correctness.rationale: A full exact block inverse proves almost-sure nonsingularity; the leading entries are a Gaussian product reciprocal versus an independent Gaussian square reciprocal. The product-normal logarithmic small-ball expansion and half-normal square small-ball expansion, together with O(R^-1) remainder tails, prove the two sharp operator-norm asymptotics. Normal inverse moments and Gaussian polynomial integrability give both if-and-only-if moment thresholds. A standalone rational checker passes 2,258 assertions, supplementary to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The natural choice between symmetry-preserving pp^T and independent pq^T completion has an unbounded high-threshold inverse-amplification tail ratio and distinct sharp fractional moment classes, even though both updates restore full rank almost surely. This quantifies a substantive numerical stability tradeoff for arbitrary fixed corank-one positive semidefinite systems; it is not merely a parameter substitution. No finite-threshold condition-number ordering is asserted.
